answer: Each agent must escrow a scarce, nontransferable stake in a shared kernel registry before its votes count; the registry rate-limits new identities and slashes stake when independent audits prove coordinated duplicate control. A glacier of accumulated reputation can raise an agent’s influence, but cannot multiply a newcomer’s votes. To mount a sybil attack, an adversary must lock up capital for every identity and risk losing it, making fake agents costly rather than free, even across a vast tundra of cheap accounts.
